steps.title: Collect and verify raw data
steps.instruction: Gather historical petroleum product consumption, lagged consumption, price, real income, household count, and urbanization rate from the listed sources (HPSF, CCPD, National Institute of Statistics, World Bank) for the period 1992‑2017 and verify consistency.

steps.title: Select predictor variables
steps.instruction: Perform stepwise regression analysis (SRA) on the collected variables using significance level, F‑to‑enter (Fe) and F‑to‑remove (Fr) criteria; retain variables that satisfy F > Fe and discard those with F < Fr.

steps.title: Construct input sequences
steps.instruction: For each retained variable Xi (i = 1…n, n = 7) build the original non‑negative sequence Xi(0) = {xi(0)(1), xi(0)(2), …, xi(0)(k)} with sample size k ≥ 4 (k = 4 for the initial CSP). X1(0) is the output (consumption), X2‑Xn(0) are the predictors.

steps.title: Apply Accumulated Generating Operation
steps.instruction: Transform each Xi(0) to its first‑order AGO sequence Xi(1) where xi(1)(t) = ∑_{m=1}^{t} xi(0)(m) for t = 2…k, producing monotonically increasing sequences.

steps.title: Compute background values
steps.instruction: Calculate the background series Z1(1)(t) = θ·X1(1)(t) + (1‑θ)·X1(1)(t‑1) for t = 2…T, using the horizontal adjustment coefficient θ (default 0.5, but may be set to 0.01‑0.99 to minimise forecast error).

steps.title: Form grey system equations
steps.instruction: Set up the differential equation dx1(1)(t)/dt + a·x1(1)(t) = ∑_{j=2}^{n} bj·xj(1)(t) + u and approximate it with the trapezoid‑based difference equation x1(0)(t) + a·Z1(1)(t) = ∑_{j=2}^{n} bj·Zj(1)(t) + u.

steps.title: Estimate coefficients by least squares
steps.instruction: Assemble matrix B and vector Y as defined in the protocol, then compute A = [ a, b2, …, bn, u ]ᵀ = (BᵀB)⁻¹ Bᵀ Y to obtain the grey parameters.

steps.title: Solve the grey differential equation
steps.instruction: Numerically evaluate x̂¹(1)(t) = x1(0)(1)·e^{a(1‑t)} + 0.5·h(t)·∑_{i=2}^{t}[ f(τ)·e^{a(τ‑t)} + f(τ‑1)·e^{a(τ‑t‑1)} ] where h(t)=1 for t ≥ 2, using the trapezoid formula.

steps.title: Apply inverse AGO to obtain forecasts
steps.instruction: Compute the predicted original values x̂¹(0)(t) = x̂¹(1)(t) ‑ x̂¹(1)(t‑1) for t ≥ 2.

steps.title: Define CSP for model parameters
steps.instruction: Create a constraint‑satisfaction problem P = (χ,D,C,R) with variables χ = {k, θ, a, b1…bn}, domains D (e.g., D(k) = {4,…,n²}, D(θ) = (0,1)), and constraints C1: 4 ≤ k < n², C2: 0 < θ < 1, C3: b1 ≠ b2 ≠ … ≠ bn. Apply the nAC3 N‑ary arc‑consistency algorithm to prune inconsistent values.

steps.title: Initialize genetic algorithm
steps.instruction: Generate a population P(t) of N = 100 chromosomes, each encoding m = 3 + n = 10 genes (k, θ, a, b1…bn) as binary strings of total length 83. Use the encoding k,θ,a,bj = L + α·(U‑L)/ (2^{β}‑1) where L/U are lower/upper bounds, α is the decimal value of the binary gene, and β is the number of bits.

steps.title: Set GA operators and parameters
steps.instruction: Configure mutation probability Pm = 1/83 (≈0.012) or lower (≤ 0.05), crossover probability Pc = 0.6, enable elitism, and define convergence precision ε = 0.05. Limit the run to a maximum of 50 generations.

steps.title: Run GA with arc‑consistency filtering
steps.instruction: For each generation: evaluate fitness (forecast accuracy), apply AC to each chromosome (treating it as a CSP) to discard infeasible genes, perform selection, crossover (Pc), mutation (Pm), and retain elite individuals. Stop when ε is reached or 50 generations elapsed.

steps.title: Sequential forecasting loop
steps.instruction:
Repeat the following until the desired horizon is covered:
1) Build GMC(1,n) with the most recent p = ? sequences (e.g., Xi(0)(1)…Xi(0)(p)).
2) Optimize k, θ, a, bj via AC‑GA and forecast the next q consumption points X̂(0)(p+1)…X̂(0)(p+q).
3) Discard the oldest p sequences, shift the window to Xi(0)(q+1)…Xi(0)(q+p), and go to step 1.
(The values of p and q are chosen by the analyst; the protocol uses the same p and q throughout.)

steps.title: Evaluate model performance
steps.instruction:
Compute accuracy metrics on the test set (2009‑2017):
- MAPE = (1/N)∑|X‑X̂|/X × 100 (thresholds: ≤0.01 perfect, ≤0.05 good, ≤0.1 acceptable, >0.1 poor)
- Correlation r (≥0.98 excellent, ≥0.95 good, ≥0.90 acceptable, <0.90 poor)
- Adjusted R² (same thresholds as r)
- RMSE = √[(1/N)∑(X‑X̂)²] (lower is better, near 0 ideal)
- AAE = (1/N)∑|X‑X̂| (lower is better)
Record CPU execution time (e.g., 97 s without AC, 5 s with AC, saving 92 s) and the generation at which convergence occurs (e.g., 34 → 13 with AC).

steps.title: Report results and compare models
steps.instruction: Present forecast curves, residuals, and the performance tables (MAPE, RMSE, AAE, r, Adj R²) for GMC(1,n), OGMC(1,n), and Sequential‑GMC(1,n)‑GA. Highlight that the sequential‑GA with AC achieves the lowest errors (e.g., MAPE ≈ 1.44 % for LPG, 0.44 % for kerosene) and fastest convergence.
